title: Forces and Motion
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Forces and Motion Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe forces as pushes and pulls; distinguish contact forces (friction) and non-contact forces (gravity); describe how forces change the motion and shape of objects. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Forces Causing Movement)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on pushes and pulls, friction, gravity and how forces change motion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Friction slows things down; gravity pulls things toward Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn an object.

  • Contact forces happen when objects touch, like friction and pushes.
  • Non-contact forces act from a distance, like gravity and magnetism.
  • Smooth surfaces like ice have little friction; rough surfaces like carpet have more.
Example

Why does a puck slide far on ice?

ice is smooth

Answer: there is little friction

Example

Which force pulls a toboggan down a hill?

it pulls toward Earth

Answer: gravity

Common mistakes

  • Thinking moving objects stop because they 'run out of force'.
  • Thinking gravity only acts on heavy objects.
  • Thinking friction is always bad.

items.q: A toy car is pushed with the same force across four surfaces: a bath towel, a polished wooden floor, carpet, ice. On which will it travel furthest?
items.e: The smoothest surface has the least friction, so the car goes furthest.

items.e: The roughest surface has the most friction, so the car stops soonest.
